item.research_question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?
item.material_system: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations
item.test_conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization
key_findings: Eight alloys were identified from 3246 initial compositions meeting criteria for Tm > 1250 °C and specific L21 phase fractions.
Alloy 1 (Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5) exhibited a yield strength of 1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C.
Alloy 8 (Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5) exhibited a yield strength of 1032 ± 10 MPa at 600 °C.
Both Alloys 1 and 8 maintained yield strengths of 607 ± 22 MPa and 643 ± 16 MPa respectively at 700 °C.
Alloy 1 contained nanoscale L21 precipitates (10–30 nm) with a number density of 2.76 × 10²²/m³ and volume fraction of 43.6 vol.%.
Alloys 2–7 formed ordered L21 antiphase domains (APDs) with volume fractions up to ~85 vol.% rather than precipitates.
The ordering transition temperature (Tc) was calculated as 1607 °C for Alloy 1 and 1997 °C for Alloy 7.
Alloys 1 and 8 outperformed traditional BCC + L21, BCC + D03, and BCC + B2 alloys in yield strength and specific yield strength.
item.mechanism: High yield strengths in Alloys 1 and 8 are attributed to precipitation strengthening where the hard L21 phase bears a larger load (load-transfer behavior) compared to the soft BCC matrix, driven by ordering strengthening (~904 MPa). The morphology (nanoscale precipitates vs. APDs) depends on the deviation from perfect L21 stoichiometry; compositions matching stoichiometry form single-phase APDs, while deviations lead to precipitates in a BCC matrix.
item.limitations: The current thermodynamic database requires improvement regarding the stability of the L21 phase, as evidenced by microstructure discrepancies between prediction and observation for Alloys 2–7. The high-throughput predictions are currently valid only in the composition range of Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.% with unchanged contents of other elements.
item.future_work: Long-period annealing on the identified alloys and quantitative characterization are necessary to improve the thermodynamic database. The high-throughput design should be coupled with the deciphered atomic occupancy rules to accelerate the discovery of advanced HEAs in multicomponent systems.
quotes: Alloys 1 and 8 exhibit high yield strengths below 700 °C (1072 ± 25 MPa at 600 °C for Alloy 1; 1032 ± 10 MPa at 600 °C for Alloy 8).
